sentences.zh: =姚南仲=姚南仲，華州下邽人。

translations.literal: Yao Nanzhong, a native of Xiaji in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nanzhong was from Xiaji in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，制科登第，授太子校書，歷高陵、昭應、萬年三縣尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he passed the special examination, was appointed collator to the crown prince, and served successively as district magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the institutional examination and was made collator to the crown prince, then served in succession as magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺，轉右補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Reminder and transferred to Right Supplementation-eradicator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Reminder and later transferred to Right Supplementation-eradicator.

sentences.zh: 大歷十三年，貞懿皇后獨孤氏崩，代宗悼惜不已，令於近城為陵墓，冀朝夕臨望於目前。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dali, Empress Zhenyi, née Dugu, died. Emperor Daizong mourned her without end and ordered a tomb built near the capital so that morning and evening he might gaze upon it before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 13 the Zhenyi Empress, Lady Dugu, died. Daizong grieved deeply and ordered a mausoleum built just outside the city so he could visit it at every hour.

sentences.zh: 南仲上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Nanzhong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝甚嘉之，賜緋魚袋，特加五品階，宣付史館。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Emperor greatly praised it, bestowed a crimson fish pouch, specially raised him five grades in rank, and ordered it announced to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor was greatly pleased, awarded him the crimson fish tally, promoted him five grades in rank, and had the document sent to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 與宰相常袞善，袞貶官，南仲坐出為海鹽縣令。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the chief minister Chang Gun. When Gun was demoted, Nanzhong was implicated and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to the chief minister Chang Gun; when Gun was demoted, Nanzhong was caught up in the affair and posted out as magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 浙江東、西道觀察使韓滉辟為推官，奏授殿中侍御史、內供奉，充支使。

translations.literal: Han Huang, observer of the Eastern and Western Zhejiang circuits, recruited him as investigating officer, memorialized to appoint him Attending Censor within the Palace and inner attendant, and commissioned him as disbursement commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, regional commissioner for eastern and western Zhejiang, took him on as investigating clerk and had him appointed attending censor and inner attendant, with responsibility for disbursements.

sentences.zh: 尋征還，歷左司兵部員外，轉郎中，遷御史中丞、給事中、同州刺史、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled, served successively as left-department assistant in the Ministry of War and then bureau director, and was promoted to censor-in-chief, recipient of edicts, prefect of Tongzhou, and observer of Shaan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled, served in the left secretariat and the War Ministry, rose to bureau director, and was appointed chief censor, recipient of edicts, prefect of Tongzhou, and commissioner for Shaan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，代李復為鄭滑節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 15 he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng and Hua.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍恃勢奪軍政，南仲數為盈珍讒毀，德宗頗疑之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Xue Yingzhen relied on his power to usurp military administration; Nanzhong was repeatedly slandered by Yingzhen, and Dezong came to doubt him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Xue Yingzhen abused his position to seize control of the command; Yingzhen slandered Nanzhong repeatedly, and Dezong grew suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，盈珍遣小使程務盈馳驛奉表，誣奏南仲陰事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yingzhen sent his petty envoy Cheng Wuying by rapid post to present a memorial falsely accusing Nanzhong of secret dealings.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen Yingzhen sent a minor aide, Cheng Wuying, by courier with a memorial falsely charging Nanzhong with covert misconduct.

sentences.zh: 南仲裨將曹文洽亦入奏事京師，伺知盈珍表中語。

translations.literal: Nanzhong's deputy general Cao Wenzha also came to the capital to report on affairs and, by watching, learned the wording of Yingzhen's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong's deputy Cao Wenzha had also gone to the capital on business and learned what Yingzhen's memorial said.

sentences.zh: 文洽私懷憤怒，遂晨夜兼道追務盈，至長樂驛及之，與同舍宿；

translations.literal: Wenzha harbored private anger and therefore pursued Wuying day and night by forced marches; at Changle Post Station he caught up with him and lodged in the same quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fuming in private, Wenzha rode day and night after Wuying, overtook him at Changle post station, and lodged with him in the same inn.

sentences.zh: 中夜殺務盈，沈盈珍表於廁中，乃自殺。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night he killed Wuying, sank Yingzhen's memorial in the privy, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he killed Wuying, dropped Yingzhen's memorial into the latrine, and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 日旰，驛吏辟門，見血流塗地，旁得文洽二緘，一告於南仲，一表理南仲之冤，且陳首殺務盈。

translations.literal: At sundown the post clerk opened the door, saw blood smeared across the ground, and beside them found two missives from Wenzha—one informing Nanzhong, one stating Nanzhong's innocence and confessing that he had killed Wuying.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening the station attendant opened the door, found blood everywhere, and discovered two letters from Wenzha—one for Nanzhong and one clearing Nanzhong's name while confessing that he had killed Wuying.

sentences.zh: 上聞其事，頗駭異之。

translations.literal: When the sovereign heard of the affair, he was greatly startled and wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of the incident, he was profoundly astonished.

sentences.zh: 南仲慮釁深，遂乞入朝。

translations.literal: Nanzhong, fearing the breach would deepen, therefore begged leave to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the scandal would deepen, Nanzhong asked permission to come to court.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「盈珍擾軍政耶？

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Does Yingzhen disturb military administration?"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong asked, "Has Yingzhen been meddling in army affairs?"

sentences.zh: 」南仲對曰：「勇珍不擾軍政，臣自隳陛下法耳。

translations.literal: Nanzhong replied: "Yongzhen does not disturb military administration; it is I who have myself destroyed Your Majesty's laws."
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong replied, "Yingzhen does not disturb military matters; I am the one who has broken Your Majesty's laws."

sentences.zh: 如盈珍輩所在有之，雖羊、杜復生，撫百姓，禦三軍，必不能成愷悌父母之政，師律善陣之制矣。

translations.literal: Where men like Yingzhen exist, even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were reborn to soothe the hundred clans and command the three armies, they surely could not achieve government as kindly parents or regulations of military discipline and good formations.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever men like Yingzhen are found, even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were brought back to life to nurture the people and lead the armies, they could not establish benevolent rule or sound military discipline.

sentences.zh: 」上默然久之。

translations.literal: The sovereign was silent for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent for a long while.

sentences.zh: 授尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年七月，終於位，年七十四，贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he died in office at the age of seventy-four; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 19 he died in office at seventy-four; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the temple name Zhen.

sentences.zh: =劉迺=劉迺，字永夷，洺州廣平人。

translations.literal: Liu Nai, style name Yongyi, a native of Guangping in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nai, courtesy name Yongyi, was from Guangping in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖武幹，武德初拜侍中，即中書侍郎林甫從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wu Gan was appointed Attendant-in-ordinary at the beginning of Wude; he was the son of the elder cousin of Zhongshu Vice Director Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wu Gan was made Attendant-in-ordinary at the start of Wude; he was a cousin once removed of Vice Director of the Secretariat Linpu.

sentences.zh: 父如璠，昫山丞，以迺貴，贈民部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ru Fan was assistant magistrate of Xushan; because of Nai's eminence he was posthumously given Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Fan had been assistant magistrate of Xushan; when Nai rose in rank, Ru Fan was posthumously made bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 迺少聰穎誌學，暗記《六經》，日數千言。

translations.literal: Nai in youth was clever and intent on learning; he memorized the Six Classics by heart and each day could recite several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Nai was bright and eager to study; he knew the Six Classics by heart and could recite several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 及長，文章清雅，為當時推重。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his writings were refined and elegant, and he was esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his prose was refined and elegant, and his contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，舉進士，尋丁父艱，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination; soon afterward he entered mourning for his father and was known for filial conduct during the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination; when his father died he observed mourning and became known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 既終制，從調選曹。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he went to the Selection Bureau for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, he reported to the Selection Bureau for appointment.

sentences.zh: 迺常以文部選才未為盡善，遂致書於知銓舍人宋昱曰：

translations.literal: Nai often considered that the Ministry of Rites' selection of talent was not yet fully adequate, and therefore sent a letter to Selection Commissioner Song Yu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Nai often felt that the Ministry of Rites did not select talent as well as it might, and wrote to Selection Commissioner Song Yu, saying:

sentences.zh: 《虞書》稱：「知人則哲，能官人則惠。

translations.literal: The Documents of Yu says: "To know men is to be wise; to be able to assign offices to men is to be benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Yu says, "To know men is wisdom; to place men in office is benevolence."

sentences.zh: 」巍巍唐、虞，舉以為難。

translations.literal: In the august age of Tang and Yu, all regarded this as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the lofty age of Tang and Yu, all regarded this as difficult.

sentences.zh: 今夫文部，既始之以掄材，終之以授位，是則知人官人，斯為重任。

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Rites begins with selecting talent and ends with conferring office; thus to know men and assign them offices is a weighty responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Rites begins by selecting talent and ends by conferring office—so knowing men and placing them in office is a weighty charge.

sentences.zh: 昔在禹、稷、臯陶之眾聖，猶曰載采有九德，考績以九載。

translations.literal: In the time of the many sages Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao, it was still said that one must gather and test the nine virtues and examine achievement over nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Even among the sages Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao, it was said that one must gather and test the nine virtues and examine achievement over nine years.

sentences.zh: 近代主司，獨委一二小冢宰，察言於一幅之判，觀行於一揖之內，古今遲速，何不侔之甚哉！

translations.literal: In recent times the chief examiners entrust everything to one or two petty chief stewards, examining words in a single sheet of judgment prose and observing conduct within one bow—how greatly ancient and modern differ in speed!
translations.idiomatic: In recent times chief examiners leave everything to one or two junior stewards, judging talent from a single examination essay and character from a single bow—how vast the gap between antiquity and the present!

sentences.zh: 夫判者，以狹詞短韻，語有定規為體，亦猶以一小冶而鼓眾金，雖欲為鼎為鏞，不可得也。

translations.literal: Judgment essays take narrow wording and short rhymes, with language bound by fixed rules as their form—like using a small furnace to smelt many metals: though one wishes to make tripods and bells, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment essays use cramped phrasing and short rhymes within fixed forms—like trying to cast tripods and bells in a small furnace: the grand result is impossible.

sentences.zh: 故曰：判之在文，至局促者。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that judgment essays in literary form are the most cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that judgment essays are the most cramped form of writing.

sentences.zh: 夫銓者，必以崇衣冠，自媒耀為賢，斯又士之醜行，君子所病。

translations.literal: In selection, candidates must elevate fine dress and self-display as marks of worth—this again is an ugly practice among scholars, what the gentleman deplores.
translations.idiomatic: At selection time candidates parade fine dress and self-promotion as proof of merit—an ugly habit among scholars that gentlemen deplore.

sentences.zh: 若引文公、尼父登之於銓廷，則雖圖書《易象》之大訓，以判體挫之，曾不及徐、庾。

translations.literal: If Duke Wen and the Master were brought before the selection hall, then though they possessed the great teachings of the classics and the Changes, constrained by the judgment form they would not equal Xu Ling and Yu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: If Duke Wen and Confucius appeared at the selection hall, their mastery of the classics and the Changes would be cut down by the judgment format and they would rank below Xu Ling and Yu Xin.

sentences.zh: 雖有至德，以喋喋取之，曾不若嗇夫。

translations.literal: Though possessing supreme virtue, if chosen for glib talk they would not equal a stingy petty clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Though possessed of supreme virtue, if chosen for glib chatter they would rank below a petty miser.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 彼幹霄蔽日，誠巨樹也，當求尺寸之材，必後於椓杙。

translations.literal: Those trees that pierce the sky and shade the sun are truly great trees, yet when one seeks timber by the foot they must come after stakes and pegs.
translations.idiomatic: Trees that pierce the clouds and shade the sun are truly great timber, yet when boards are measured by the foot they rank behind stakes and pegs.

sentences.zh: 龍吟武嘯，誠希聲也，若尚頰舌之感，必下於蛙黽。

translations.literal: The dragon's cry and the tiger's roar are truly rare sounds; if one esteems the sensation of cheek and tongue, one must rank below frogs and toads.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon's cry and the tiger's roar are truly rare voices; if glib talk is prized, one must rank below frogs and toads.

sentences.zh: 觀察之際，猶不悲夫！

translations.literal: At the moment of observation, is it not still lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: When one considers this, is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 執事慮過龜策，文合雅誥，豈拘以瑣瑣故事，曲折因循哉？

translations.literal: Your Lordship's deliberations surpass the tortoise and yarrow stalks, your writing accords with the elegant decrees—how could you be bound by petty precedents and twisted compliance?
translations.idiomatic: Your deliberations surpass divination, your prose matches the classical decrees—surely you need not be bound by petty precedent and roundabout compliance?

sentences.zh: 誠能先資以政事，次征以文學，退觀其理家，進察其臨節，則厖鴻深沈之事，亦可以窺其門戶矣！

translations.literal: If you truly can first assess by administrative affairs, next examine by literary learning, withdraw to observe how they manage the household, and advance to inspect how they meet crises, then even vast and profound matters may be glimpsed through their doorway!
translations.idiomatic: If you first weigh administrative ability, then literary accomplishment, observe how candidates manage their households in private life and how they meet crises in public office, even the weightiest matters may be judged through their doorway.

sentences.zh: 其載，補剡縣尉，改會稽尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed, filling the post of district defender of Shan County, then transferred to defender of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed defender of Shan County and later transferred to defender of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 宣州觀察使殷日用奏為判官，宣慰使李季卿又以表薦，連授大理評事、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Yin Riyong, observer of Xuanzhou, memorialized to appoint him as administrative aide; the pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him by memorial, and he was successively given the posts of Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Riyong, commissioner of Xuanzhou, had him appointed as aide; pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him, and he was successively made evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏令巡覆江西，多所蠲免。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to have him tour and review Jiangxi, and many levies were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Liu Yan had him tour and review Jiangxi, and many taxes were remitted.

sentences.zh: 改殿中侍御史、檢校倉部員外、民部郎中，並充浙西留後。

translations.literal: He was changed to Attending Censor within the Palace, Acting Assistant in the Granaries Bureau, and Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently served as acting commissioner of Western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attending censor within the palace, acting assistant in the Granaries Bureau, and bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently served as acting commissioner of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 佐晏征賦，頗有裨益，晏甚任之。

translations.literal: Assisting Yan in collecting taxes, he was of considerable benefit, and Yan greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In assisting Yan with tax collection he proved highly useful, and Yan relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 大歷十二年，元載既誅，以迺久在職，召拜司門員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dali, after Yuan Zai had been executed, because Nai had long served in office he was summoned and appointed Assistant Director in the Bureau of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 12, after Yuan Zai was executed, Nai was summoned to court and appointed assistant director in the Bureau of Gates because of his long service.

sentences.zh: 十四年，崔祐甫秉政，素與迺友善。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Cui Youfu held power; he had long been on friendly terms with Nai.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen Cui Youfu held power; he had long been friendly with Nai.

sentences.zh: 會加郭子儀尚父，以冊禮久廢，至是復行之。

translations.literal: It happened that Guo Ziyi was given the title of Sublime Preceptor; because the enfeoffment rites had long been abandoned, they were now revived.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was then given the title Sublime Preceptor; the enfeoffment rites had long fallen into disuse and were now revived.

sentences.zh: 祐甫令兩省官撰冊文，未稱旨；

translations.literal: Youfu ordered officials of the two departments to draft the enfeoffment document, but it did not please the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Youfu had officials of the two departments draft the enfeoffment document, but it did not please the throne;

sentences.zh: 召迺至閣草之，立就。

translations.literal: Nai was summoned to the pavilion to draft it, and it was completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Nai was summoned to the pavilion to draft it and finished immediately.

sentences.zh: 詞義典裁，祐甫嘆賞久之。

translations.literal: The wording and meaning were classical and measured; Youfu sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was classical and measured; Youfu admired it at length.

sentences.zh: 數日，擢為給事中，尋遷權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Within several days he was promoted to Recipient of Edicts, and soon transferred to Acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was promoted to recipient of edicts and soon made acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 及楊炎、盧杞為相，意多醜正，以故五歲不遷。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi became chief ministers, their minds were much set against the upright, and for this reason he went five years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi became chief ministers, they disliked upright men, and for this reason he went five years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 建中四年夏，但真拜而已。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Jianzhong he received only a formal appointment and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianzhong 4 he received only a formal appointment and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 其冬，涇師作亂，駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: That winter the Jing army mutinied and the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jing army mutinied and the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 迺臥疾在私第，賊泚遣使以甘言誘之，乃稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Nai lay ill in his private residence; the rebel Zhu Ci sent envoys with sweet words to entice him, and he therefore claimed his illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Nai lay ill at home; the rebel Zhu Ci sent envoys with flattering words to entice him, and he claimed his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 又令其偽宰相蔣鎮自來招誘，迺托喑疾，灸灼遍身。

translations.literal: Ci also had his false chief minister Jiang Zhen come in person to recruit him; Nai pleaded loss of speech and had moxibustion burns over his entire body.
translations.idiomatic: Ci also sent his puppet chief minister Jiang Zhen to recruit him in person; Nai feigned muteness and had moxibustion burns applied all over his body.

sentences.zh: 鎮再至，知不可劫脅，乃嘆息曰：「鎮亦嘗忝列曹郎，茍不能死，以至於斯，寧以自辱膻腥，復欲汙穢賢哲乎？

translations.literal: When Zhen came a second time and knew he could not be coerced, he sighed and said: "Zhen too once held office among the bureau directors. If one cannot die when one should, one comes to this—how could I further disgrace myself with foul meat and then try to defile a worthy sage?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen came again and saw he could not be coerced, he sighed and said, "I too once served among the bureau directors. If one cannot die when one should, one comes to this—how could I further disgrace myself and then try to defile a worthy man?"

sentences.zh: 」歔欷而退。

translations.literal: He sobbed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及聞輿駕再幸梁州，乃自投於床，搏膺呼天，因是危惙，絕食數日而卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: When he heard the imperial carriage had again gone to Liangzhou, he threw himself upon his bed, beat his breast, and cried to Heaven; because of this he fell into mortal collapse, abstained from food for several days, and died at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the emperor had again gone to Liangzhou, he threw himself on his bed, beat his breast, and cried to Heaven; he then fell critically ill, refused food for several days, and died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，聞迺之忠烈，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital and heard of Nai's loyal martyrdom, he posthumously gave him Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital and heard of Nai's loyal death, he posthumously made him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子伯芻。

translations.literal: His son was Bo Chu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Bo Chu.

sentences.zh: 伯芻，字素芝，登進士第，誌行修謹。

translations.literal: Bo Chu, style name Suzhi, passed the jinshi examination; his conduct and aspirations were cultivated and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chu, courtesy name Suzhi, passed the jinshi examination; his conduct was cultivated and careful.

sentences.zh: 淮南杜佑辟為從事，府罷，屏居吳中。

translations.literal: Du You of Huainan recruited him as staff officer; when the office was abolished he lived in seclusion in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Du You of Huainan took him on as staff officer; when the office closed he lived in seclusion in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 久之，征拜右補闕，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Right Supplementation-eradicator, then promoted to Assistant in the Ministry of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned as Right Supplementation-eradicator and later promoted to assistant in the Ministry of Guests.

sentences.zh: 以過從友人飲噱，為韋執誼密奏，貶虔州掾曹，復為考功員外郎裴垍善其應對機捷，遷考功郎中、集賢院學士，轉給事中。

translations.literal: Because he went out drinking and jesting with friends, Wei Zhiyi secretly memorialized against him and he was demoted to staff officer in Ganzhou. Later, as Assistant in the Bureau of Merit Pei Ji admired his quick and nimble responses in audience; he was promoted to Bureau Director in Merit, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and transferred to Recipient of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Because he went out drinking and jesting with friends, Wei Zhiyi secretly memorialized against him and he was demoted to staff officer in Ganzhou. Later Pei Ji, assistant in the Bureau of Merit, admired his quick wit in audience; he was promoted to bureau director in Merit, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and then recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 裴垍罷相，為太子賓客，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was removed as chief minister and made Mentor to the Heir Apparent; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was removed as chief minister and made mentor to the heir apparent; he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫復入相，與垍宿嫌，不加贈官；

translations.literal: Li Jifu again entered office as chief minister; he had an old grudge against Ji and did not grant him posthumous office;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu again became chief minister; he had an old grudge against Ji and did not grant him a posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 伯芻上疏論之，贈垍太子少傅。

translations.literal: Bo Chu submitted a memorial arguing the point, and Ji was posthumously given Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chu submitted a memorial on the matter, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 伯芻妻，垍從姨也。

translations.literal: Bo Chu's wife was Ji's younger cousin on the maternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chu's wife was Ji's younger cousin on the maternal side.

sentences.zh: 或讒於吉甫，此以論奏。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to Jifu; this was why he submitted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to Jifu; that was why he submitted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 伯芻懼，亟請散地，因出為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Bo Chu was afraid and urgently begged for a post without heavy duties; he was therefore sent out as prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chu was afraid and urgently asked for a lighter post; he was sent out as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，裴度擢為刑部侍郎，俄知吏部選事。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, Pei Du promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, and soon he was in charge of selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu died, Pei Du promoted him to vice minister of justice, and soon he was in charge of selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，以左常侍致仕，卒，年六十一，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he retired as Left Regular Attendant, died at the age of sixty-one, and was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 10 he retired as Left Regular Attendant, died at sixty-one, and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 伯芻風姿古雅，涉學，善談笑，而動與時適，論者稍薄之。

translations.literal: Bo Chu's bearing was ancient and elegant; he was versed in learning and skilled at conversation and laughter, yet his actions often suited the moment, and critics slightly looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chu had an ancient and elegant bearing, was learned, and was skilled at conversation, yet his actions often suited the moment, and critics held him somewhat lightly.

sentences.zh: 子寬夫，登進士第，歷諸府從事。

translations.literal: His son Kuanfu passed the jinshi examination and served successively as staff officer in various offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuanfu passed the jinshi examination and served as staff officer in various offices.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，入為監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era he entered office as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoli he entered office as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言曰：「近日攝祭多差王府官僚，位望既輕，有乖嚴敬。

translations.literal: He once submitted a statement, saying: "Recently acting sacrifices have often assigned princely establishment officials; their rank and standing are already light, which violates solemn reverence."
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a statement, saying, "Recently acting sacrifices have often assigned princely establishment officials; their rank is too low, which violates solemn reverence."

sentences.zh: 伏請今後攝太尉，差尚書省三品已上及保傅賓詹等官；

translations.literal: I humbly request that hereafter for acting Grand Marshal, officials of third rank and above from the Department of State Affairs and tutors, mentors, guests, and aides be assigned;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that hereafter for acting Grand Marshal, officials of third rank and above from the Department of State Affairs and tutors, mentors, guests, and aides be assigned;

sentences.zh: 如人少，即令丞郎通攝之。

translations.literal: if men are few, then let vice directors and bureau directors jointly act in their place.
translations.idiomatic: if there are too few men, let vice directors and bureau directors jointly act in their place.

sentences.zh: 」俄轉左補闕。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation-eradicator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation-eradicator.

sentences.zh: 少列陳岵進註《維摩經》，得濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Junior Attendant Chen Hu submitted a commentary on the Vimalakirti Sutra and received the post of prefect of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Attendant Chen Hu submitted a commentary on the Vimalakirti Sutra and was made prefect of Hao.

sentences.zh: 寬夫與同列，因對論之，言岵因供奉僧進經以圖郡牧。

translations.literal: Kuanfu and his colleagues, during an audience discussion of the matter, said that Hu had presented the sutra through a court-attending monk in order to seek a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu and his colleagues, during an audience discussion, said that Hu had presented the sutra through a court monk in order to obtain a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敬宗怒謂宰相曰：「陳岵不因僧得郡，諫官安得此言，須推排頭首來。

translations.literal: Jingzong angrily told the chief ministers: "Chen Hu did not obtain his prefecture through a monk—how can the remonstrance officials say such a thing? The ringleader must be identified and brought forward."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong angrily told the chief ministers, "Chen Hu did not obtain his prefecture through a monk—how can the remonstrance officials say such a thing? The ringleader must be identified and brought forward."

sentences.zh: 」寬夫奏曰：「昨論陳岵之時，不記發言前後，唯握筆草狀，即是微臣。

translations.literal: Kuanfu submitted: "When Chen Hu was discussed yesterday, I do not remember who spoke before or after; I alone held the brush and drafted the memorial—that was I, your humble servant."
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu submitted, "When Chen Hu was discussed yesterday, I do not remember who spoke before or after; I alone held the brush and drafted the memorial—that was I."

sentences.zh: 今論事不當，臣合當罪。

translations.literal: Now that the discussion was improper, I ought to bear the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If the discussion was improper, I ought to bear the guilt.

sentences.zh: 若尋究推排，恐傷事體。

translations.literal: If you investigate and identify the ringleader, I fear it will harm the proper conduct of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If you investigate and identify the ringleader, I fear it will harm the proper conduct of affairs.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其引過，欣然釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him for taking blame upon himself and gladly released the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for taking blame upon himself and gladly released the matter.

sentences.zh: 寬夫弟端夫，為太常博士，駁韋綬謚議知名。

translations.literal: Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and became famous for refuting the posthumous-title deliberation on Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and became famous for refuting the posthumous-title deliberation on Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 寬夫子允章、煥章。

translations.literal: Kuanfu's sons were Yunzhang and Huanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu's sons were Yunzhang and Huanzhang.

sentences.zh: 允章登進士第，累官至翰林學士承旨、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yunzhang passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Academician Expositor of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang passed the jinshi examination and rose to expositor of the Hanlin Academy and vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 咸通九年，知貢舉，出為鄂州觀察使、檢校工部尚書，後遷東都留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xiantong he supervised the examinations, was sent out as observer of Ezhou and Acting Minister of Works, and later transferred to be Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 9 he supervised the examinations, was sent out as commissioner of Ezhou and acting minister of works, and later became defender of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯洛陽，允章不能拒，賊不之害，坐是廢於家。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Luoyang, Yunzhang could not repel him; the rebels did not harm him, and for this he was dismissed and kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao struck Luoyang, and Yunzhang was unable to hold the city; the rebels spared his life, but he was stripped of office and sent home for it.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of an illness.

sentences.zh: =袁高=袁高，字公頤，恕己之孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Gao, style name Gongyi, was the grandson of Suji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gao, courtesy name Gongyi, was a grandson of Yuan Suji.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，慕名節。

translations.literal: From youth he was generous and ardent, and admired reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man he was bold and high-minded, and he revered men of honor and principle.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，累辟使府，有贊佐裨益之譽。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly summoned to commissioner offices, and had a reputation for effective assistance and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly in regional headquarters, and won praise for the help he gave his superiors.

sentences.zh: 代宗登極，征入朝，累官至給事中、御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to court and rose through successive posts to Supervising Censor and Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daizong took the throne, he was called to the capital and advanced step by step to supervising censor and attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，擢為京畿觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, he was promoted to Metropolitan Circuit Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 he was promoted to metropolitan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以論事失旨，貶韶州長史，復拜為給事中。

translations.literal: Because his remonstrances missed the emperor's intent, he was demoted to Long Administrator of Shaozhou, then reappointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Because his policy remonstrances displeased the throne, he was demoted to chief administrator of Shaozhou, then appointed supervising censor again.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，德宗復用吉州長史盧杞為饒州刺史，令高草詔書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Emperor Dezong again employed Lu Qi, Long Administrator of Jizhou, as Prefect of Raozhou, and ordered Gao to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 Emperor Dezong again appointed Lu Qi, former chief administrator of Jizhou, prefect of Raozhou, and told Gao to draft the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 高執詞頭以謁宰相盧翰、劉從一曰：「盧杞作相三年，矯詐陰賊，退斥忠良。

translations.literal: Gao took the draft preamble and called on chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi, saying, "Lu Qi served as chancellor for three years, perversely deceitful and secretly wicked, driving away and rejecting the loyal and worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took the draft edict in hand and went to see chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi. "Lu Qi was chancellor for three years," he said, "a man of twisted fraud and hidden villainy who drove out the loyal and worthy."

sentences.zh: 朋附者咳唾立至青雲、睚眥者顧盼已擠溝壑。

translations.literal: Those who joined his faction reached the clouds with a cough or spit; those who incurred his slightest resentment were, with a glance, squeezed into ravines and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: His followers rose to the highest offices on his slightest favor; anyone who crossed him was, with a look, cast down into ruin.

sentences.zh: 傲很明德，反易天常，播越鑾輿，瘡痍天下，皆杞之為也。

translations.literal: He arrogantly defied bright virtue, reversed the natural order, drove the imperial carriage into exile, and left the whole realm scarred and wounded—all of this was Lu Qi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned enlightened virtue, overturned Heaven's order, drove the imperial carriage into exile, and left the empire bleeding—Lu Qi did all of this.

sentences.zh: 爰免族戮，雖示貶黜，尋已稍遷近地，若更授大郡，恐失天下之望。

translations.literal: Though he was spared clan extermination and shown demotion and exile, he was soon gradually moved back to posts nearer the capital; if he is now given a large prefecture, I fear it will disappoint the hopes of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared execution of his clan and only sent into exile, yet he has already been moved back toward the capital; if he is now given a great prefecture, the empire will lose hope.

sentences.zh: 惟相公執奏之，事尚可救。

translations.literal: Only if you, Chancellor, firmly submit a memorial on this can the matter still be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Only if you, my lords, firmly remonstrate can this still be set right.

sentences.zh: 」翰、從一不悅，改命舍人草之。

translations.literal: Han and Congyi were displeased and ordered a drafting secretary to rewrite it.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Congyi were displeased and had a palace draftee compose the edict instead.

sentences.zh: 詔出，執之不下，仍上奏曰：「盧杞為政，窮極兇惡。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Gao held it and would not promulgate it, and submitted a memorial saying, "In governing, Lu Qi has exhausted every extreme of villainy and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came out, Gao refused to promulgate it and submitted a memorial: "In office Lu Qi has reached the utmost in wickedness and cruelty."

sentences.zh: 三軍將校，願食其肉；

translations.literal: Officers of the three armies would gladly eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The officers of all three armies would gladly eat his flesh.

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，嫉之若讎。

translations.literal: The hundred ministers and officials hate him as they would an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister and official in the court hates him like a mortal enemy.

sentences.zh: 」遺補陳京、趙需、裴佶、宇文炫、盧景亮、張薦等上疏論奏。

translations.literal: Remonstrance-supplement officials Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others submitted memorials arguing the case.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementary remonstrance officials Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others also submitted memorials on the matter.

sentences.zh: 次日，又上疏。

translations.literal: The next day they submitted again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they submitted again.

sentences.zh: 高又於正殿奏云：「陛下用盧杞獨秉鈞軸，前後三年，棄斥忠良，附下罔上，使陛下越在草莽，皆杞之過。

translations.literal: Gao again memorialized in the main hall, saying, "Your Majesty employed Lu Qi alone to hold the state seals; for three years altogether he cast out the loyal and worthy, attached himself to inferiors and deceived superiors, and caused Your Majesty to be driven into the wilds—all of this was Lu Qi's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Gao again remonstrated in the main hall: "Your Majesty put Lu Qi alone at the helm of state; for three years he cast out the loyal, flattered those below and deceived those above, and drove Your Majesty into exile—all of this was Lu Qi's fault."

sentences.zh: 且漢時三光失序，雨旱不時，皆宰相請罪，小者免官，大者刑戮。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Han times when the three luminaries lost their proper order and rains and droughts came at wrong seasons, it was always the chancellor who confessed guilt—lesser faults led to removal from office, greater ones to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in Han times when the sun, moon, and stars fell out of order and rain and drought came untimely, the chancellor always took the blame—lesser cases meant dismissal, greater ones execution.

sentences.zh: 杞罪合至死，陛下好生惡殺，赦杞萬死，唯貶新州司馬，旋復遷移。

translations.literal: Lu Qi's crimes deserved death; Your Majesty loves life and hates killing, pardoned him from myriad deaths, and only demoted him to Militia Vice Director of Xinzhou, yet soon moved him again.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi's crimes merited death; Your Majesty, loving life and hating bloodshed, spared him from ten thousand deaths and only demoted him to militia vice director of Xinzhou, yet soon moved him again.

sentences.zh: 今除刺史，是失天下之望。

translations.literal: Now appointing him prefect is to fail the hopes of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Now to make him prefect is to betray the empire's hopes.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖意裁擇。

translations.literal: I humbly submit myself to the sacred decision.
translations.idiomatic: I leave the decision to Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 」上謂曰：「盧杞有不逮，是朕之過。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "Where Lu Qi fell short, that was my fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "Where Lu Qi fell short, the fault was mine."

sentences.zh: 」復奏曰；

translations.literal: Gao memorialized again, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gao submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「盧杞奸臣，常懷詭詐，非是不逮。

translations.literal: "Lu Qi is a treacherous minister who constantly harbors deceit and fraud—it is not a matter of falling short.
translations.idiomatic: "Lu Qi is a treacherous minister who constantly plots deceit; this is not a matter of falling short."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕已有赦。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have already issued a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already pardoned him."

sentences.zh: 高曰：「赦乃赦其罪，不宜授刺史。

translations.literal: Gao said, "A pardon pardons his crimes; it is not fitting to grant him a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "A pardon forgives his crimes; it does not entitle him to a prefecture."

sentences.zh: 且赦文至優黎民，今饒州大郡，若命奸臣作牧，是一州蒼生，獨受其弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, the pardon text was entirely generous toward the common people; now Raozhou is a large prefecture—if a treacherous minister is ordered to govern it, the common people of that entire prefecture alone will suffer the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the pardon spoke of mercy for the people; Raozhou is a great prefecture, and if a traitorous minister is sent to govern it, the people of that whole region alone will bear the harm."

sentences.zh: 望引常參官顧問，並擇謹厚中官，令采聽於眾。

translations.literal: I hope You will summon regular court officials for consultation and also select prudent and honest palace eunuchs to gather and hear from the populace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty consult the regular officials at court and also choose prudent palace eunuchs to gather the people's opinion."

sentences.zh: 若億兆之人異臣之言，臣當萬死。

translations.literal: If the countless multitudes disagree with my words, I deserve ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: If the countless people of the empire disagree with me, I deserve death ten thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 」於是，諫官爭論於上前，上良久謂曰：「若與盧杞刺史太優，與上佐可乎？

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrance officials debated before the emperor; after a long while the emperor said, "If making Lu Qi prefect is too generous, would making him senior administrator be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the remonstrance officials argued before the throne, and after a long silence the emperor said, "If prefect is too generous an appointment for Lu Qi, would senior administrator suffice?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「可矣！

translations.literal: They said, "That will do!
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "That would be acceptable!"

sentences.zh: 」遂追饒州制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Raozhou appointment edict was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The edict appointing him to Raozhou was then withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遣使宣慰高云：「朕思卿言深理切，當依卿所奏。

translations.literal: The next day he sent an envoy to proclaim consolation to Gao, saying, "I find your words deeply reasoned and forceful; I shall act according to your memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor sent an envoy to comfort Gao, saying, "Your words were deeply reasoned and forceful; I shall follow your memorial."

sentences.zh: 」太子少保韋倫、太府卿張獻恭等奏：「袁高所奏至當，高是陛下一良臣，望加優異。

translations.literal: Former Crown Prince Junior Tutor Wei Lun, Chamberlain of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Zhang Xiangong, and others memorialized, "What Yuan Gao memorialized was entirely appropriate; Gao is a good minister of Your Majesty—I hope he may receive special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun, Grand Chamberlain Zhang Xiangong, and others submitted a memorial: "Yuan Gao's remonstrance was entirely justified; he is a worthy minister of Your Majesty, and we hope he will receive exceptional reward."

translations.literal: [Memorial ends.]
translations.idiomatic: The memorial concluded.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，上以關輔祿山之後，百姓貧乏，田疇荒穢，詔諸道進耕牛，待諸道觀察使各選揀牛進貢，委京兆府勸課民戶，勘責有地無牛百姓，量其地著，以牛均給之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, because after the An Lushan rebellion in the Guanzhong region the common people were impoverished and fields lay fallow and uncultivated, the emperor decreed that circuits should send plow oxen; each circuit observation commissioner was to select oxen and submit them as tribute, and the Metropolitan Prefecture was charged with urging households in agricultural work, investigating common people who had land but no oxen, measuring their registered holdings, and distributing oxen evenly to them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2, seeing that after the An Lushan rebellion the people of Guanzhong were destitute and their fields lay waste, the emperor ordered every circuit to send plow oxen; each observation commissioner was to select and present them, and the Metropolitan Prefecture was to urge farming among the households, identify landholders without oxen, measure their registered holdings, and distribute oxen to them in proportion.

sentences.zh: 其田五十畝已下人，不在給限。

translations.literal: Those with fifty mu of land or less were not within the scope of distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Households with fifty mu of land or less were excluded from the distribution.

sentences.zh: 高上疏論之：「聖慈所憂，切在貧下。

translations.literal: Gao submitted a memorial arguing, "What the sage compassion worries about lies precisely with the poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: Gao submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's concern lies above all with the poor."

sentences.zh: 有田不滿五十畝者尤是貧人，請量三兩家共給牛一頭，以濟農事。

translations.literal: Those with less than fifty mu of land are especially the poor—I request that two or three households be allotted one ox together to help their farming.
translations.idiomatic: Those with less than fifty mu are precisely the poorest; I ask that two or three such households be given one ox together so they can keep farming."

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官，年六十，中外嘆惜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in office at age sixty; inside and outside the court lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office at the age of sixty, and the court and the country mourned him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗朝，宰臣李吉甫嘗言高之忠鯁，詔贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzong's reign, Chancellor Li Jipu once spoke of Gao's loyal forthrightness, and an edict posthumously awarded him Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Xianzong, Chancellor Li Jipu praised Gao's loyal bluntness, and an edict posthumously made him minister of rites.

sentences.zh: =段平仲=段平仲，字秉庸，武威人。

translations.literal: Duan Pingzhong, style name Bingyong, was a native of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzhong, courtesy name Bingyong, was from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 隋人部尚書段達六代孫也。

translations.literal: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Duan Da, Minister of Personnel of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Duan Da, Sui minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、李復相繼鎮淮南，皆表平仲為掌書記。

translations.literal: Du You and Li Fu successively governed Huainan, and both recommended Pingzhong as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Du You and Li Fu, who governed Huainan in succession, both recommended Pingzhong as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 復移鎮華州、滑州，仍為從事。

translations.literal: When Fu moved to govern Hua and Hua Prefectures, Pingzhong continued as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu was transferred to Hua and Hua Prefectures, Pingzhong went with him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 入朝為監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 平仲磊落尚氣節，嗜酒傲言。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was open and upright, valued integrity, loved wine, and spoke boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was open and magnanimous, prized integrity, loved wine, and spoke with bold bluntness.

sentences.zh: 時德宗春秋高，多自聽斷。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Dezong was advanced in years and often decided matters himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Dezong was old and often decided affairs in person.

sentences.zh: 由是庶務壅隔，事或不理，中外畏上嚴察，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Consequently routine affairs were blocked and some matters went unresolved; inside and outside the court feared the emperor's stern scrutiny, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Routine business piled up and some matters went untended; inside and outside the court feared the emperor's severity, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 平仲嘗謂人曰：「主上聰明神武，臣下畏懼不言，自循默耳。

translations.literal: Pingzhong once said to others, "The sovereign is intelligent and martially resplendent; the ministers keep silent out of fear—that is simply conforming in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong once told others, "The sovereign is intelligent and formidable; the ministers say nothing because they are afraid—that is simply keeping silent out of habit."

sentences.zh: 如平仲一得召見，必當大有開悟。

translations.literal: If someone like Pingzhong were once summoned to audience, he would surely bring great enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: If someone like me were once summoned to audience, I would surely open his eyes wide."

sentences.zh: 」貞元十四年，京師旱，詔擇御史、郎官各一人，發廩賑恤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, the capital suffered drought; an edict chose one censor and one bureau official each to open granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 14 the capital suffered drought; the emperor ordered one censor and one secretary to open the granaries and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 平仲與考功員外陳歸當奉使，因辭得對，乃入近禦座，粗陳本事。

translations.literal: Pingzhong and Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chen Gui were to serve on the mission; taking leave to respond, he came near the imperial seat and briefly stated the facts of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong and Vice Director of Personnel Chen Gui were chosen for the mission; when they took leave to respond, Pingzhong came near the imperial seat and briefly stated the purpose of the mission.

sentences.zh: 上察平仲意有所蓄，以歸在側不言。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived that Pingzhong had something stored up to say, but because Gui was at his side he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that Pingzhong had more to say, but because Gui was standing beside him he held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 及奏事畢退，平仲獨不退，欲有奏啟；

translations.literal: When the report of business was finished and they withdrew, Pingzhong alone did not withdraw, wishing to submit a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When their report was finished and they withdrew, Pingzhong alone did not leave, intending to speak further.

sentences.zh: 上因兼留歸問之，聲色甚厲，雜以他語。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore also kept Gui and questioned him, his voice and expression very stern, mixing in other talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore kept Gui as well and questioned him, his voice and face very stern, interspersing other remarks.

sentences.zh: 平仲錯愕，都不得言因誤稱其名。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was flustered and could not get a word out, and in error called him by name.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was thrown into confusion and could say nothing; in his confusion he even addressed the emperor by name.

sentences.zh: 上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and shouted him out of the hall.

sentences.zh: 平仲蒼黃，又誤趨禦障後，歸下階連呼，乃得出。

translations.literal: Pingzhong panicked and again mistakenly rushed behind the imperial screen; Gui called repeatedly from the bottom of the steps before he could get out.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong, panicked, blundered behind the imperial screen; only when Gui called repeatedly from the foot of the steps was he able to get out.

sentences.zh: 由是坐廢七年，然亦因此名顯。

translations.literal: On this account he was dismissed and idle for seven years, yet also on this account his fame became conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was dismissed and passed seven years without office, yet on that very account his name became famous.

sentences.zh: 後除屯田膳部二員外郎、東都留守判官，累拜右司郎中。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministries of Public Works and of Court Ceremonies, and staff judge of the Eastern Capital garrison command; he rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made vice director in the ministries of public works and court ceremonies and staff judge to the eastern capital garrison, and rose step by step to vice director of the right department.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was transferred to Remonstrance Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he was made remonstrance advisor.

sentences.zh: 內官吐突承璀為招討使，征鎮州，無功而還。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Tuhu Chencui served as campaign commander, attacked Zhen Prefecture, and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Tuhu Chencui served as campaign commander against Zhen Prefecture and returned without success.

sentences.zh: 平仲與呂元膺抗疏論列，請加黜責。

translations.literal: Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying submitted strong memorials criticizing this and requested further demotion and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong and Lü Yuanying submitted forceful memorials denouncing him and asking that he be further demoted and punished.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 自在要近，朝廷有得失，未嘗不論奏，時人推其狷直。

translations.literal: Once he was in a key position near the throne, whenever the court had gains or losses he never failed to submit memorials; contemporaries praised his uncompromising integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held an important post near the throne, he never failed to speak whenever the court erred or did well, and men of the time praised his uncompromising honesty.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書左丞，以疾改太子左庶子卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; due to illness he was changed to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died in that post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; because of illness he was moved to left mentor of the heir apparent and died in that office.

sentences.zh: =薛存誠=薛存誠，字資明，河東人。

translations.literal: Xue Cuncheng, style name Ziming, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父勝，能文，嘗作《拔河賦》，詞致瀏亮，為時所稱。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was skilled at literature; he once wrote "Rhapsody on Tug-of-War," whose wording was polished and bright, and was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng was a capable writer; he once composed "Rhapsody on Tug-of-War," whose language was fluent and bright, and was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 存誠進士擢第，累辟使府，入朝為監察御史，知館驛。

translations.literal: Cuncheng was selected in the jinshi examination, was repeatedly summoned to commissioner offices, entered court as Investigating Censor, and supervised postal stations.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly in regional headquarters, entered court as an investigating censor, and oversaw the postal relay stations.

sentences.zh: 元和初，王師討劉辟，郵傳多事，上特令中官為館驛使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, when imperial troops campaigned against Liu Pi, postal relay stations were much burdened; the emperor specially ordered palace eunuchs to serve as postal station commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe, when imperial armies marched against Liu Pi, the postal system was overburdened, and the emperor specially appointed palace eunuchs as postal commissioners.

sentences.zh: 存誠密表論奏，以為有傷公體。

translations.literal: Cuncheng submitted a secret memorial arguing that this harmed the dignity of the public institution.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng submitted a secret memorial arguing that this damaged public propriety.

sentences.zh: 會諫官亦論奏，上乃罷之。

translations.literal: When remonstrance officials also submitted memorials, the emperor then abolished the practice.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrance officials also remonstrated, the emperor abolished the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中侍御史，遷度支員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor and promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and promoted to vice director of revenue.

sentences.zh: 裴垍作相，用為起居郎，轉司勛員外、刑部郎中、兼侍御史、知雜事，改兵部郎中、給事中。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji became chancellor, Cuncheng was employed as Recorder of the Emperor's Actions; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors, Director of the Ministry of Justice, concurrently Attendant Censor overseeing miscellaneous matters, then changed to Director of the Ministry of War and Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji became chancellor, Cuncheng was made recorder of the emperor's actions; he then served as vice director of honors, director of justice, attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business, and finally director of war and supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 瓊林庫使奏占工徒太廣，存誠以為此皆奸人竄名，以避征役，不可許。

translations.literal: The commissioner of the Qionlin treasury reported that laborer registrations were excessively broad; Cuncheng held that these were all treacherous men who hid under false names to evade conscription and corvée—they could not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of the Qionlin treasury reported that registered laborers were too numerous; Cuncheng argued that these were scoundrels hiding under false names to evade conscription and corvée, and that the practice could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 咸陽縣尉袁儋與軍鎮相競，軍人無理，遂肆侵誣，儋反受罰。

translations.literal: Xianyang County Lieutenant Yuan Dan disputed with a military garrison; the soldiers were without reason and thereupon wantonly slandered and encroached, and Dan in turn was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianyang county lieutenant Yuan Dan clashed with a military garrison; the soldiers were in the wrong yet wantonly slandered and encroached on him, and Yuan Dan was punished instead.

sentences.zh: 二敕繼至，存誠皆執之。

translations.literal: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng held both and would not promulgate them.
translations.idiomatic: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng refused to promulgate either.

sentences.zh: 上聞甚悅，命中使嘉慰之，由是擢拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he was greatly pleased, ordered a palace envoy to commend and console him, and on this account promoted him to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was greatly pleased, sent a palace envoy to praise and comfort him, and on that account promoted him to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 僧鑒虛者，自貞元中交結權倖，招懷賂遺，倚中人為城社，吏不敢繩。

translations.literal: The monk Jianxu, from the Zhenyuan era onward, cultivated connections with the powerful and favored, solicited and accepted bribes, relied on palace insiders as his ramparts and altars, and officials did not dare restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Jianxu, from the Zhenyuan era on, cultivated the powerful and the favored, solicited bribes, relied on palace insiders as his protection, and officials did not dare touch him.

sentences.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。

translations.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When private misconduct in the households of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated, arrested, and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 存誠案鞫得奸贓數十萬，獄成，當大辟。

translations.literal: Cuncheng investigated and interrogated the case and found treacherous bribes amounting to several hundred thousand; when the case was complete, the penalty was death.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng investigated the case and found illicit gains of several hundred thousand; when the trial was complete, the sentence was death.

sentences.zh: 中外權要，更於上前保救，上宣令釋放，存誠不奉詔。

translations.literal: Powerful figures inside and outside the court repeatedly pleaded for his rescue before the emperor; the emperor proclaimed an order to release him, but Cuncheng did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful men inside and outside the court repeatedly interceded for him before the emperor; the emperor ordered his release, but Cuncheng refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 明日，又令中使詣臺宣旨曰：「朕要此僧面詰之，非赦之也。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor again had a palace envoy go to the censorate and proclaim, "I wish to interrogate this monk face to face—it is not a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor again sent a palace envoy to the censorate with this order: "I wish to question this monk in person; this is not a pardon."

sentences.zh: 」存誠附中使奏曰：「鑒虛罪款已具，陛下若召而赦之，請先殺臣，然後可取。

translations.literal: Cuncheng attached his memorial to the envoy's report, saying, "Jianxu's criminal confession is complete; if Your Majesty summons and pardons him, please kill me first—and only then may you take him.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng sent a memorial through the envoy: "Jianxu's guilt is fully established; if Your Majesty summons and pardons him, kill me first—then take him."

sentences.zh: 不然，臣期不奉詔。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I pledge not to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will not obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其有守，從之，鑒虛竟笞死。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his steadfastness, acceded, and Jianxu was ultimately beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity, agreed, and Jianxu was finally beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 洪州監軍高重昌誣奏信州刺史李位謀大逆，追赴京師。

translations.literal: Hongzhou Military Supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely memorialized that Xin Prefecture Prefect Li Wei plotted great treason; Li was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhou military supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely reported that Xin Prefecture prefect Li Wei was plotting treason, and Li Wei was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上令付仗內鞫問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him handed over to the inner palace guard for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that he be handed over to the inner guard for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 存誠一日三表，請付位於御史臺。

translations.literal: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in one day requesting that Li Wei be entrusted to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in a single day asking that Li Wei be entrusted to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及推案無狀，位竟得雪。

translations.literal: When the investigation found no evidence, Li Wei was ultimately cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was investigated and no evidence was found, Li Wei was finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 未幾，再授給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 數月，中丞闕，上思存誠前效，謂宰相持憲無以易存誠，遂復為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Several months later, when the Attendant Censor post was vacant, the emperor recalled Cuncheng's previous service and told the chancellors that in upholding the law none could replace Cuncheng; he was thereupon again made Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, when the attendant censor post fell vacant, the emperor remembered Cuncheng's earlier service and told the chancellors that in upholding the law no one could replace him; Cuncheng was therefore made attendant censor again.

sentences.zh: 未視事，暴卒。

translations.literal: Before he assumed the duties of office, he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even taken up the duties of office, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 憲宗深惜之，贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong deeply regretted it and posthumously awarded him Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong deeply regretted his death and posthumously made him vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 存誠性和易，於人無所不容，及當官禦事，即確乎不拔，士友以是稱重之。

translations.literal: Cuncheng's nature was gentle and easy; toward people he bore no intolerance, but when holding office and confronting affairs he was firmly unyielding—scholars and friends therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cuncheng was mild and accommodating toward all, yet in office he was immovable; scholars and colleagues esteemed him for it.

sentences.zh: 子廷老。

translations.literal: His son was Tinglao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tinglao.

sentences.zh: 廷老謹正有父風，而性通銳。

translations.literal: Tinglao was careful and upright with his father's manner, yet his nature was acute and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao was careful and upright like his father, yet his nature was sharp and quick.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中為右拾遺。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era he served as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoli he served as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 敬宗荒恣，宮中造清思院新殿，用銅鏡三千片、黃白金薄十萬番。

translations.literal: Jingzong was dissolute and reckless; in the palace they built a new hall in Qingsi Courtyard, using three thousand bronze mirrors and one hundred thousand sheets of gold and silver leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was dissolute and reckless; the palace built a new hall in Qingsi Courtyard, using three thousand bronze mirrors and one hundred thousand sheets of gold and silver leaf.

sentences.zh: 廷老與同僚入閣奏事曰：「臣伏見近日除拜，往往不由中書進擬，或是宣出。

translations.literal: Tinglao and his colleagues entered the inner court to report on affairs, saying, "Your servant has observed that recent appointments and dismissals often do not come through the Secretariat's recommendations but are issued by imperial announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao and his colleagues reported at court, saying, "We have observed that recent appointments often bypass the Secretariat and are issued by imperial announcement."

sentences.zh: 伏恐綱紀漸壞，奸邪恣行。

translations.literal: I humbly fear that discipline will gradually collapse and treachery will run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that discipline will gradually collapse and the wicked will run rampant."

sentences.zh: 」敬宗厲聲曰：「更諫何事？

translations.literal: Jingzong said sharply, "What else do you remonstrate about?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said sharply, "What else do you remonstrate about?"

sentences.zh: 」舒元褒對曰：「近日宮中修造太多。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanbao replied, "Recently there has been too much construction in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanbao replied, "Recently there has been too much construction in the palace."

sentences.zh: 」上色變曰：「何處修造？

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed and he said, "Where is there construction?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed and said, "Where is there construction?"

sentences.zh: 」元褒不能對，廷老進曰：「臣等職是諫官，凡有所聞，即合論奏。

translations.literal: Yuanbao could not answer; Tinglao stepped forward and said, "Our duty as remonstrance officials is that whatever we hear, we ought to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao could not answer; Tinglao stepped forward and said, "As remonstrance officials, whatever we hear we ought to report."

sentences.zh: 莫知修造之所，但見運瓦木絕多，即知有用。

translations.literal: We do not know where the construction is, but seeing tiles and timber transported in great quantity, we know it is being used.
translations.idiomatic: We do not know where the construction is, but seeing vast quantities of tiles and timber transported, we know it is underway."

sentences.zh: 乞陛下勿罪臣言。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to punish my words.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to punish my words."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「所奏已知。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your report is noted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your report is noted."

sentences.zh: 」尋加史館修撰。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Historiography Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉秉權，惡廷老言太切直。

translations.literal: At that time Li Fengji held power and hated Tinglao's words for being too blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Fengji held power and hated Tinglao for speaking too bluntly.

sentences.zh: 鄭權因鄭註得廣州節度，權至鎮，盡以公家珍寶赴京師以酬恩地。

translations.literal: Zheng Quan obtained the Guangzhou commandery through Zheng Zhu; when Quan reached his post he sent all the public treasures to the capital to repay the favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan obtained the Guangzhou commandery through Zheng Zhu; when Quan reached his post he sent all public treasures to the capital to repay the favor.

sentences.zh: 廷老上疏請按權罪，中人由是切齒。

translations.literal: Tinglao submitted a memorial requesting investigation of Quan's crimes; palace eunuchs therefore gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao submitted a memorial requesting investigation of Quan's crimes; palace eunuchs therefore hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 又論逢吉黨人張權輿、程昔範不宜居諫列，逢吉大怒。

translations.literal: He also argued that Fengji's partisans Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan were unfit to hold remonstrance posts; Fengji was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Fengji's partisans Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan were unfit for remonstrance posts; Fengji was greatly enraged.

sentences.zh: 廷老告滿十旬，逢吉乃出廷老為臨晉縣令。

translations.literal: When Tinglao's leave of one hundred days was complete, Fengji sent Tinglao out as magistrate of Linjin County.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinglao's leave of one hundred days was complete, Fengji posted him out as magistrate of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he entered office as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he entered office as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，以本官充翰林學士，與同職李讓夷相善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, in his original office he was made Hanlin Academician and was on good terms with his colleague Li Rangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4, in his original office he was made Hanlin academician and was on good terms with his colleague Li Rangyi.

sentences.zh: 廷老之入內署，讓夷薦挈之。

translations.literal: Tinglao's entry into the inner secretariat was due to Rangyi's recommendation and support.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao's entry into the inner secretariat was due to Rangyi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 廷老性放逸嗜酒，不持檢操，終日酣醉，文宗知之不悅。

translations.literal: Tinglao's nature was unrestrained and he loved wine; he did not restrain his conduct and was drunk all day—Wenzong knew this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao was unrestrained and loved wine; he did not restrain his conduct and was drunk all day—Wenzong knew and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 五年，罷職，守本官，讓夷亦坐廷老罷職，守職方員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was removed from office and kept his original post; Rangyi also because of Tinglao was removed and kept his post as Assistant in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was removed from the Hanlin post and kept his original office; Rangyi was also removed because of Tinglao and kept his post as assistant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 廷老尋拜刑部員外郎，轉郎中，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Tinglao was soon appointed Assistant in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to Bureau Director, and promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglao was soon made assistant in the Ministry of Justice, rose to bureau director, and was promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 開成三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 廷老當官舉職，不求虛譽，侃侃於公卿之間，甚有正人風望。

translations.literal: When Tinglao held office and performed his duties, he did not seek empty reputation; among the high ministers he spoke frankly and had the bearing of an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: In office Tinglao sought no empty reputation; among high ministers he spoke frankly and had the bearing of an upright man.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 子保遜，登進士第，位亦至給事中。

translations.literal: His son Baoxun passed the jinshi examination and also rose to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoxun passed the jinshi examination and also rose to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 保遜子昭緯，乾寧中為禮部侍郎，貢舉得人，文章秀麗。

translations.literal: Baoxun's son Zhaowei, in the Qianning era was Vice Minister of Rites; his examinations selected worthy men and his writings were elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun's son Zhaowei, in the Qianning era was vice minister of rites; his examinations selected worthy men and his writings were elegant.

sentences.zh: 為崔胤所惡，出為磎州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was hated by Cui Yin and was sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was hated by Cui Yin, was sent out as prefect of Qi, and died there.

sentences.zh: =盧坦=盧坦，字保衡，河南洛陽人，其先自范陽徙焉。

translations.literal: Lu Tan, style name Baoheng, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan, courtesy name Baoheng, was from Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父巒，贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Luan was posthumously given Prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luan was posthumously made prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 坦嘗為義成軍判官，節度使李復疾篤，監軍使薛盈珍慮變，遽封府庫，入其麾下五百人於使牙，軍中恟々；

translations.literal: Tan once served as administrative aide of the Yicheng army; when Military Commissioner Li Fu's illness was grave, Army Supervisor Xue Yingzhen feared trouble, hastily sealed the treasury, and brought five hundred of his own troops into the commissioner headquarters—the army was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Tan once served as aide to the Yicheng army; when commissioner Li Fu lay gravely ill, army supervisor Xue Yingzhen feared trouble, hastily sealed the treasury, and brought five hundred of his own troops into headquarters—the army was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 坦密言於盈珍促收之。

translations.literal: Tan secretly told Yingzhen to withdraw them quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Tan secretly urged Yingzhen to withdraw them quickly.

sentences.zh: 及復卒，坦護喪歸東都。

translations.literal: When Fu died, Tan escorted the coffin back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, Tan escorted the coffin back to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 後為壽安令。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was magistrate of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 時河南尹征賦限窮，而縣人訴以機織未就；

translations.literal: At that time the Henan prefect was pressing the tax deadline to the limit, while the county people pleaded that their looms were not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Henan prefect was pressing the tax deadline to the limit, while county residents pleaded that their weaving was not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 坦請延十日，府不許。

translations.literal: Tan requested a ten-day extension; the prefecture did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan requested a ten-day extension; the prefecture refused.

sentences.zh: 坦令戶人但織而輸，勿顧限也，違之不過罰令俸耳。

translations.literal: Tan ordered the households simply to weave and deliver payment without regard to the deadline—violating it would only mean deducting the magistrate's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Tan ordered households simply to weave and pay when ready, ignoring the deadline—if they missed it, only the magistrate's salary would be fined.

sentences.zh: 既成而輸，坦亦坐罰，由是知名。

translations.literal: When the weaving was done and delivered, Tan also accepted punishment, and on this account became known.
translations.idiomatic: When weaving was finished and delivered, Tan also accepted punishment, and on this account became known.

sentences.zh: 累遷至庫部員外郎、兼侍御史、知雜事。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Assistant in the Ministry of the Treasury, concurrently Attendant Censor overseeing miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant in the Ministry of the Treasury, concurrently attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 會李锜反，有司請毀锜祖父廟墓。
